description: Project-specific overrides for aioson git:guard. allowPaths affects path rules only; contentAllowPaths is a legacy whole-file bypass; prefer scoped contentAllowRules with an audit reason.

contentAllowRules.reason: SQLite FTS5 tokenize configures Unicode text segmentation; it is not a credential assignment.
Test fixture writes the YOUR_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY placeholder into a temp aioson-models.json to exercise the missing-key guidance path; it is not a credential.
Template provider entries contain explicit YOUR_*_API_KEY placeholders; the file instructs users to replace them and is not a credential store.
Jev privacy tests use named synthetic password and api_key values to prove redaction before transport; they are never real credentials.
Jev CLI tests use a YOUR_OPENROUTER_API_KEY placeholder and a runtime-secret sentinel in an isolated fixture; neither is a credential.
Jev relevance tests use provider placeholders and synthetic route values to verify config loading and fallback behavior; they are not credentials.
Jev review tests use a root-config placeholder and synthetic provider setup in temporary projects; they are not credentials.
The Jev tutorial displays YOUR_*_API_KEY placeholders in JSON examples so readers can configure their own provider; no credential is present.
The orchestration tutorial displays the crsr_SUA_CHAVE_AQUI placeholder to explain Cursor environment setup; no credential is present.
The orchestration-with-Jev tutorial shows an aioson-models.json example whose api_key holds the environment variable name OPENROUTER_API_KEY; no credential is present.
Jev key-resolution tests use a named synthetic OpenRouter-style literal to prove an api_key written in the models file is used as written; it is never a real credential.

Jev key-resolution tests assign named synthetic OpenRouter-style values to OPENROUTER_API_KEY in temporary .env files and env maps to prove .env and environment precedence; they are never real credentials.
The Jev setup steps print an aioson-models.json example whose api_key holds the environment variable name OPENROUTER_API_KEY, which the config resolves from the environment; no credential is present.
Deployer guidance names the ?access_token= query parameter as a URL shape Traefik access logs would record; no credential value is present.
